query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy is a solid refrigeration working medium that exhibits a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor load-bearing integrity and tends to crack. What single intervention could increase its integrity while preserving caloric performance in these operating regimes? State one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, predicted integrity and caloric outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, applicable field, pressure, temperature, and loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit results that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a small fraction (e.g., 1-3 at%) of Ti as a substitutional element into the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy matrix will increase its load-bearing integrity (fracture toughness and resistance to cracking) without significantly diminishing its caloric performance under applied magnetic field and pressure-field operation.
generation.intervention: Partial substitution of Ti (1-3 at%) for one or more constituent elements (e.g., replacing a portion of Mn or Fe) in the alloy composition
generation.conditions: Applied magnetic fields up to 2 T, hydrostatic pressures up to 1 GPa, temperatures between 250 K and 350 K, mechanical loading relevant to refrigeration device operation
generation.structural_mediator: Ti addition promotes grain boundary strengthening and ductility via solid solution effects, possibly reducing intergranular cracking and improving toughness
generation.mechanism: Ti atoms act as grain boundary stabilizers and ductility enhancers, mitigating stress concentrations and crack propagation while maintaining the entropy-driven phase stability and magnetocaloric/pressure-caloric response
generation.predicted_outcome: The modified alloy will exhibit increased fracture toughness and resistance to cracking (e.g., >20% improvement in measured toughness or reduction in crack density) with caloric performance (ΔS, ΔT under field/pressure) remaining within 90% of the original alloy's values
generation.baseline: Unmodified (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy, known to have poor load-bearing integrity and high caloric response
generation.boundary: Intervention is valid for Ti substitution levels up to 3 at%; higher levels may degrade caloric performance or phase stability. Applicable for polycrystalline samples under refrigeration-relevant field, pressure, and temperature regimes.
generation.uncertainty: There is moderate uncertainty regarding the exact Ti substitution site and its effect on phase stability; insufficient evidence on the impact of Ti on magnetocaloric and barocaloric properties in this specific alloy system.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: (1) original alloy, (2) alloy with 2 at% Ti substituted for Mn. Subject both to identical mechanical loading, magnetic field (up to 2 T), and pressure (up to 1 GPa) cycles at 300 K. Measure fracture toughness, crack density, and caloric response (ΔS, ΔT).
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If Ti-substituted alloy does not show at least 10% improvement in fracture toughness or exhibits >10% reduction in caloric response relative to the original alloy, the hypothesis is falsified.
